items.title: CLA is marked as an unreviewed draft

findings.title: Contributor Licence Agreement is committed as an unreviewed draft
findings.evidence: > **Draft — to be reviewed by a legal professional.**
findings.explanation: CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template require every contributor to sign this CLA, and README relies on it to keep dual licensing possible, but the document itself is marked as an unreviewed draft. This does not restrict distribution of the extension (the code is GPL-3.0-or-later with a full LICENSE), so it is not an admission blocker, but contributors are being asked to sign terms the author has not finalised.
findings.suggestion: Have the CLA reviewed and remove the draft banner before enforcing it on pull requests.

findings.title: CLA is marked as an unreviewed draft
findings.evidence: > **Draft — to be reviewed by a legal professional.**
findings.explanation: CLA.md, which contributors are asked to sign, says it has not been reviewed by a lawyer. Contributors may be unsure what they are granting, and the project's dual-licence model depends on this text. This does not affect distribution under GPL-3.0, which is covered by the full LICENSE file.
findings.suggestion: Have the CLA reviewed before the dual-licence offer is relied on, or remove the draft banner once it is approved.

items.title: Catalog entry tracks branch 'main' while the author's notes describe an unreleased pre-release on another branch

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks branch 'main' while the author's notes describe an unreleased pre-release on another branch
findings.evidence:
- v1.0.0 pre-release (branch `release`, from 3a7458d = Phase 2, no Phase 3):
  Parts 0-10 of the user's to-do list, done in order, stopping after each
  for testing in Slicer. Phase 3 work continues on `master` and is merged
  after the release (Part 10). Nothing is pushed publicly, tagged or put
findings.explanation: The entry sets scm_revision to "main", so whatever is on main at install time is what users get, and the reviewed commit 30e57a6 cannot be pinned from the entry. CLAUDE.md says the v1.0.0 release is on branch `release` and that nothing is to be published or put into a pull request until the author types GO RELEASE. Whether main currently holds the approved release is unclear, so the code users receive may not match what was reviewed or released.
findings.suggestion: Ask the author to confirm which commit is the intended release, and pin scm_revision to that commit or a tag in the catalog entry.

items.title: Extra test scripts are not registered with CMake, so ctest only runs the in-file test class

findings.title: Extra test scripts are not registered with CMake, so ctest only runs the in-file test class
findings.explanation: OsteotomyCuts/CMakeLists.txt registers the unittest subclass inside OsteotomyCuts.py (line 33) and adds the Testing subdirectory, but Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only contains a commented-out registration referring to a non-existent ${MODULE_NAME}ModuleTest.py. Consequently run_headless_tests.py, run_benchmark.py and run_real_models.py are never installed or executed by the extension build/ctest, so the 87 tests and the benchmark quoted in RELEASE_NOTES.md are not exercised by the index's automated build.
findings.suggestion: Register the headless runner (or the test class it drives) with slicer_add_python_unittest so the extension build actually runs the tests, and drop the stale commented line.

findings.title: Test registration commented out in Testing/Python
findings.explanation: OsteotomyCuts/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only has the test line commented out, so no module-specific ctest is registered. The main module CMakeLists still runs slicer_add_python_unittest on OsteotomyCuts.py when BUILD_TESTING is set, so the impact is limited.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dead line or register the headless test runner as a ctest.

items.title: Developer/AI-assistant notes file with local paths is committed to the public repository

findings.title: Developer/AI-assistant notes file with local paths is committed to the public repository
findings.evidence:
- Windows 11. Project: C:\Dev\OsteotomyCuts
- 3D Slicer 5.13.0 (preview build, 2026-06-30, r34833), installed for all users
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a working-notes file for an AI coding assistant: it records the author's local Windows paths, the release workflow ("Nothing is pushed publicly, tagged or put into a pull request until the user types exactly: GO RELEASE.") and instructions such as "SAFETY_NOTE and the Help / Acknowledgement texts are the user's exact wording: do not reword them." These are instructions to the author's own tooling, not to reviewers, and I found no attempt to influence review or to conceal behaviour; the file is untrusted content that I did not act on. It is only an information-disclosure/hygiene issue.
findings.suggestion: Move CLAUDE.md out of the published repository (or into a git-ignored local file) so local paths and internal workflow notes are not shipped.

items.title: Only external process invocation is a local git query, verified benign

findings.title: Only external process invocation is a local git query, verified benign
findings.evidence:
result = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=os.path.dirname(__file__),
                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
                        creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0))
findings.explanation: The provenance feature records the module's git commit. The call uses an argument list (no shell), a fixed command, a 5 s timeout and a working directory inside the extension, and failures are swallowed into "unknown". No user input reaches it, so there is no command-injection path; recorded here because it is the only process spawn in the module.

findings.title: Local git helper runs a subprocess once per session
findings.evidence:
result = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=os.path.dirname(__file__),
                                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
findings.explanation: moduleGitHash runs `git rev-parse` in the module's folder with a 5 s timeout to record provenance. It is read-only and local, and it falls back to 'unknown' on error. It is noted for transparency only.
findings.suggestion: No change required. Optionally drop the subprocess call from the shipped module.

items.title: Whole module implemented in one 7,396-line Python file

findings.title: Whole module implemented in one 7,396-line Python file
findings.explanation: All geometry, GUI, provenance and test code lives in OsteotomyCuts.py (408 KB, 7,396 lines). This is not a defect and does not affect users, but it makes review and maintenance harder and means the test class is shipped inside the module script.
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting the pure-geometry logic into a separate module file installed by CMake, keeping the ScriptedLoadableModule classes in OsteotomyCuts.py.
